findings: B0 scope kernel is double-seeded: the start terminal is seeded, popped-and-discarded, then re-pushed via BOTH terminal guards; for start==end the start row is scanned twice (stale re-scan). Duplicate incidences on the ORIGIN row therefore converge to the cheap value; the staged-scan observable (last eligible wins) is only visible on downstream rows. Both facts pinned (golden bytes + downstream construction).

B0 scope kernel has NO bounds checking (numba default). A first-draft tie fixture pointed an incidence at the destination tail; the compiled kernel read past the end of adjacency_pointer (undefined but deterministic-looking). Fixture fixed to a well-formed graph; recorded here because candidate kernels must NOT rely on the same UB.
fastmath comparison lowering is observable in the NaN domain: the vectorized mask admitted a NaN weight while the scalar seed guard rejected NaN — hazard bytes recorded, not normalized.

The A2 sentinel rounding hazard is constructible without extreme weights: cutoff = 2^53 makes the typed init b = 1 + cutoff round to exactly R, and the compiled retained filter then KEEPS the unreachable destination whose adjusted distance equals R.

F2 stale-scratch (no dd_buf/pd_buf reset between ODs) is PROVEN INERT on this corpus: gradient finite-column sets coincide and each scatter overwrites all finite columns, so outputs AND scratch states stay byte-identical (test_f2_stale_scratch_is_inert_on_corpus_documented). The reset obligation for F2I is enforced by this journal evidence plus code review, not output bytes.
limitations_and_gaps: L2 chronology (per-turn/per-iteration ordering on the observed workloads) is OUT OF SCOPE for H03 as executed: the turn-aware kernel path (_accumulate_od_flow_turns) is NOT covered by traces or the golden battery; turns=False in the flow fixture. If the campaign later enables turns, H03 needs a supplement.

Metric trace equivalence (gexp/glog) is established through B0's own compiled _decay/reach_gravity_knn_access callables — the numba exp implementation is compared against itself on traced sequences, NOT against a Python replica of exp. numba-exp bit-equality with numpy exp was probed once and matched, but that probe is not a contract.

np.argsort tie behavior in F2 tree orders is pinned only on the tie patterns present in the corpus (probe-matched numpy-vs-numba); a tie pattern outside the corpus could in principle order differently — golden bytes, not the trace, are the contract there.

Trace-vs-compiled float sums carry the documented max_ulp=4 allowance (fastmath reassociation); exact bit equality of a REPLICA is not achievable in general and is NOT required by VALIDATION — candidate comparisons remain byte-exact.

The compiled scope kernel reading adjacency_pointer out of bounds (missing boundscheck) was observed with a malformed fixture; production builders never emit such graphs, so the corpus pins well-formed graphs only.
